messages:
alice: Heads-up — I'm working through onboarding a new Private deployment customer who wants us to integrate with their GCP Cloud KMS. Questions: what minimum IAM do our control-plane service accounts need, where should the keyring live (customer project vs our infra), and how do we wire audit logs back to them? :thinking:
ben: For Private we usually recommend the keyring in the customer's project (customer retains control). Grant our control-plane SA only the encrypter/decrypter role on the specific key: `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter`. Avoid project-level roles.
maria: Agree. Also add `roles/cloudkms.viewer` to the key ring if we need to enumerate keys, but prefer scoped bindings on the `cryptoKey` resource.
dave: Quick example binding we've used:```gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/PROJECT/locations/us-central1/keyRings/REDACTED --member="serviceAccount:private-control@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"```
alice: Thanks. What about cross-project impersonation — customer doesn't want to create service accounts in their project, they asked whether we can impersonate from our control plane into their project. Is that allowed?
ben: You can do cross-project, but best practice is customer creates a dedicated SA in their project and grants `serviceAccountTokenCreator` to our control plane SA for impersonation. That way customer keeps lifecycle control. Example: customer SA `kms-client@customer-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com` -> grant `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` to `serviceAccount:private-control@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` on that SA.
maria: Note that impersonation still requires explicit least-priv roles on the key. Impersonated SA must have the KMS binding too. So two-step: (1) bind KMS role to customer SA, (2) allow our control plane SA to impersonate that SA.
dave: For locations — pick the keyring location that matches customer data residency (e.g., `us-central1`, `europe-west1`). Try to avoid multi-location if they need strict region residency.
eng-infra-bot: FYI — checklist item added to onboarding: "verify kms key location, kms IAM bindings, and audit log sink".
alice: How do we handle audit logs visibility? They want to see access logs for decrypt operations in their project.
ben: Cloud Audit Logs for KMS are project-level. If the key is in the customer project, they already get ADMIN/ACCESS logs for the key. If we impersonate, the audit entry shows the impersonated SA (good for traceability). Recommend they set up a Logs Router sink to their logging project or BigQuery for retention/compliance.
maria: Also enable CMEK-specific audit logs: `DATA_ACCESS` and `ADMIN_ACTIVITY` for Cloud KMS. Confirm they have the right logs retention and alerts.
alice: Envelope encryption — do we do envelope encryption with a customer KEK? I.e., data encrypted with a data key, wrapped by customer's KMS key.
dave: Yes. For Private we generate ephemeral DEKs (data encryption keys) on the host and call `projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/*:encrypt` to wrap the DEK. Store wrapped DEK with the object. That avoids repeated KMS calls for every datastore operation.
ben: Important: use `cryptoKeyVersions` state and rotation policy. When rotating the KEK, we re-wrap DEKs lazily: keep old key versions available to decrypt older wrapped DEKs, then rotate and start wrapping new DEKs with new version. Add a periodic rewrap job if customer wants proactive rewrap.
maria: Add this to ops playbook: "verify key version policy before key destruction, ensure no key is destroyed while versions still referenced by wrapped DEKs".
alice: Any tests we should run to validate setup before go-live?
dave: Smoke checklist: 1) Attempt encrypt/decrypt as customer SA from within their project, 2) Attempt impersonation token flow from our control plane and encrypt/decrypt, 3) Verify Cloud Audit Log entries show expected principal and methodName `google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Encrypt` / `Decrypt`, 4) Confirm sink delivers logs to customer's destination.
ben: Shareable snippet for token impersonation test:```# get short-lived token from our control plane SA impersonating customer SA
gcloud iam service-accounts impersonate kms-client@customer-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=customer-project --impersonate-service-account= kms-client@customer-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com --format=json
# then call KMS encrypt with that token (use gcloud or REST)```
alice: Good. One more: rotation cadence suggestions? Customer asked for recommended schedule.
maria: Recommend rolling keys every 90-365 days depending on sensitivity. For highly regulated data push shorter. Document their SLA for rewrap windows.
dave: And document emergency rotation playbook: 1) create new key version, 2) start new wraps, 3) monitor errors, 4) if rollback needed, switch back to previous version and re-wrap as needed.
security-bot: Incident note — last 30 days no KMS permission anomalies detected for `private-control` service account. :white_check_mark:
alice: Perfect — I'll assemble this into the onboarding doc and send to the customer. If anyone has an audit log sample to attach (redacted), please DM me. :thumbsup:
ben: I'll drop a sanitized log sample into the onboarding doc later today. :eyes:
